parts.label: Photon thermal-energy scale kBT
parts.help: Use the question’s kBT scale at 10¹² K, not the blackbody mean 2.701kBT. Polarization counting does not derive the photon mean energy.

parts.label: Nonrelativistic particle number density
parts.help: Dilute nonrelativistic gas; one internal state, g = 1, kBT ≪ mc². Dimensional constants and T are positive; μ is real.

parts.label: Initial neutron-to-proton ratio
parts.help: Neglect electron/neutrino chemical potentials and use the kBT energy scale. A ratio near one is an intended estimate.

parts.label: Estimated T₁
parts.help: Use kBT₁ ≈ 0.8 MeV (or 0.79 MeV threshold); not a weak-rate freeze-out calculation.

parts.label: Neutron-to-proton ratio at T₁
parts.help: The worked estimate rounds this ratio to 0.20.

parts.label: Estimated T₂
parts.help: Use kBT₂ ≈ mₑc² = 0.51 MeV; an estimate of pair-abundance suppression, not exact loss of chemical equilibrium.

parts.label: Deuterium equilibrium ratio nD/(np nn)
parts.help: Single-state convention; B_D is the positive binding energy 2.24 MeV in consistent units. Spin multiplicities are not included.

parts.label: Numerical-equation right-hand side (set equal to 1)
parts.help: u is the numerical value of kBT in keV; ηB = 6.1×10⁻¹⁰, Xp ≈ 1, XD/Xn ≈ 1. Use the coefficient precision in the solution.

parts.label: Low-temperature root T₃
parts.help: Select the low-temperature root near kBT₃ = 69.1 keV, not the unrelated high-temperature root.

parts.label: Coefficient ζ
parts.help: Uniform Newtonian sphere; ρ is mass-equivalent density.

parts.label: Curvature term ξ
parts.help: a is the positive scale factor; k is signed curvature, c > 0.

parts.label: Dust exponent p in energy density proportional to aᵖ
parts.help: Enter the result in the displayed unit, without a unit suffix.

parts.label: Radiation exponent p in energy density proportional to aᵖ
parts.help: Enter the result in the displayed unit, without a unit suffix.

parts.label: Temperature exponent p in T proportional to aᵖ
parts.help: Radiation domination with fixed relativistic particle content.

parts.label: Temperature ratio T(t₁)/T(t₂)
parts.help: Flat radiation-dominated Universe; Big Bang at t = 0; both times positive.

parts.label: Temperature at matter–radiation equality
parts.help: Separate matter-dominated power law from equality to recombination.

parts.label: Helium mass fraction
parts.help: Enter a fraction, not percent. Rounded r₁ = 0.20, Δt ≈ 290 s, half-life 612 s; all surviving neutrons enter helium; neglect baryonic mass differences.

parts.label: Baryon counting and decay reasoning
parts.help: Check comoving baryon counting and the neutron-decay derivation against the solution; only the final fraction is checked automatically.
